title: 3.4: A CMOS Operational Amplifier Achieving ±5.8µV 3σ Offset and ±88nV/°C 3σ Offset Drift Using an on-Chip Heater-Based Self-Trimming Technique
problem: MOS-input operational amplifiers are attractive for high-impedance sources but suffer from high offset voltage (±45µV 3σ) and large offset drift (±330nV/°C 3σ) compared to bipolar opamps. Dynamic offset cancellation (chopping/autozeroing) adds complexity and power; conventional 2-temperature trimming requires expensive test equipment and cannot correct field drift.
motivation: Precision analog signal conditioning demands low offset and minimal drift over temperature and time, especially for portable/implantable devices where field-level trimming and minimal post-packaging calibration are essential.
method: An on-chip heater-based self-trimming technique performs room-temperature trim calibration to correct MOS-input opamp offset, enabling field-deployable drift correction. The heater generates thermal gradients used during trim operation without requiring external test equipment, reducing offset to ±5.8µV (3σ) and drift to ±88nV/°C (3σ).
key_novelty: On-chip heater-based self-trimming enabling room-temperature offset and drift correction without expensive dual-temperature test equipment or complex dynamic cancellation.
contributions: Reduces offset voltage from ±45µV to ±5.8µV (3σ) – 7.8× improvement
Reduces offset drift from ±330nV/°C to ±88nV/°C (3σ) – 3.75× improvement
Enables field-deployable trim correction via on-chip heater
Simplifies manufacturing by eliminating dual-temperature trim requirement
baselines: Prior MOS-input opamp with room-temp trim (±45µV, ±330nV/°C)
limitations: Not discussed; power overhead of on-chip heater, trim convergence time, and reliability of repeated trimming cycles not characterized.
primary_theme: On-chip heater trim for precision opamp offset correction
